items.title: Pure-core burn-alert evaluator over usage-sweep session rows
items.context: New packages/main/src/core/usage-burn-alert.ts: evaluate SweepSessionRow[] against injected thresholds (nowMs and thresholds passed in; no process.env or Date.now inside, matching the usage-sweep pure-core contract). Flags a session when transcript file size exceeds the byte threshold, cumulative input tokens exceed the token threshold (codex: last cumulative total_token_usage input; claude: summed input + cacheRead + cacheCreation), or the session is older than the age threshold while still recently active. Read-only: stat only, never writes.

happy.desc: evaluateBurnAlerts flags a codex session whose file size exceeds the byte threshold (strictly greater), returning a finding with reason=file-size naming the session file and exceeded threshold
evaluateBurnAlerts flags a codex session whose last cumulative total_token_usage inputTokens exceeds the token threshold (strictly greater), returning reason=input-tokens
evaluateBurnAlerts flags a claude session whose summed (inputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheCreationInputTokens) exceeds the token threshold, returning reason=input-tokens
evaluateBurnAlerts flags a session whose firstTimestamp is older than ageDays while the session mtime falls inside the recent-activity scan window, returning reason=session-age
evaluateBurnAlerts returns an empty array for rows that are all below every threshold
A single session can trip multiple reasons simultaneously (e.g. file-size AND input-tokens); all triggered reasons appear in the finding
Findings are returned in a deterministic order (stable sort by session file or sessionId) regardless of input row order

edge.desc: A session with usage exactly AT the threshold (not strictly greater) is NOT flagged; only strictly-greater trips the alert
A session with null usage (unknown) is never flagged for input-tokens, even when other thresholds are set
A session with null or unparseable firstTimestamp is never flagged for session-age
A codex session with inputTokens=0 and a claude session with all-zero usage fields are not flagged for input-tokens
fileSizeOf injection: when fileSizeOf is not provided the evaluator stats the file; when fileSizeOf IS provided it uses the injected function (test seam for OS-temp fixtures)
An empty rows array returns an empty findings array without error
A session whose firstTimestamp is within ageDays (recent session, not old) is never flagged for session-age even if the file is very large

adversarial.desc: The module does NOT import Date.now or process.env anywhere; nowMs and thresholds are injected arguments -- verified by source grep showing zero Date.now/process.env references in the file
The module does NOT import from core/usage-ledger (independence contract inherited from usage-sweep); verified by source grep
evaluateBurnAlerts never writes to the filesystem: calling it with real session paths leaves those files byte-identical (zero-writes assertion on mtime+size snapshot before/after)
A session row whose file path does not exist on disk (stale/deleted transcript) does not throw; the file-size check gracefully skips or reports 0
Rows with NaN, Infinity, or negative token counts do not cause the evaluator to throw or produce corrupt findings

items.title: Env-tunable threshold resolver with conservative defaults
items.context: Resolver maps an env record to thresholds: LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_FILE_MB (default 100), LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_INPUT_TOKENS (default 100000000), LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_AGE_DAYS (default 7), LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_RECENT_HOURS (default 48, scan window; 0 disables the doctor burn scan). Pure function of the env record so it is testable; handlers pass process.env.

items.title: lattice doctor host-burn advisory section
items.context: doctor reuses sweepCodexSessions/sweepClaudeProjects (read-only) over the recent-activity window and prints a prominent advisory warning per flagged session naming the session file, cwd, and cumulative tokens, plus which thresholds tripped. Advisory-only: no gate, no gateEvidence, plain doctor exit code unchanged. JSON mode gets a hostBurnScan object. doctor() becomes async; existing smoke call sites updated.

items.title: usage_sweep --alert exit-nonzero mode
items.context: usage_sweep gains an --alert boolean: the report is computed and printed as today, alert evaluation runs over the swept rows, flagged sessions are listed, and the CLI exits non-zero when any alert fired (recover_evidence dispatch pattern: print result first, then throw) so a cron job can drive notifications. --alert performs zero writes and stays effectively readOnly for ownership/activity/hook classification.

items.title: Fixture-driven burn-alert smoke wired into the validate suite
items.context: New packages/main/src/tasks/usage-burn-alert-smoke.ts driven by OS temp fixtures (never real ~/.codex or ~/.claude): threshold boundary cases (at vs over), env resolver defaults and overrides, doctor section rendering (flagged and clean), --alert exit-code behavior via the real CLI, zero-writes assertion. Wired into the same validate/test entry points as usage-sweep-smoke.
